record.title: Makai Jr.'s covering-minimum conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K\in\mathcal{K}^n$ be a convex body and let $\Lambda\in\mathcal{L}^n$ be a lattice. Let $\mu_1(K,\Lambda)$ denote the first covering minimum. **Makai Jr.'s conjecture.** One has

$$
\mu_1(K,\Lambda)^n\operatorname{vol}(K)\geq\frac{n+1}{2^n n!}\det(\Lambda),
$$

and equality can occur only when $K$ is a simplex. If $K$ is origin-symmetric, then

$$
\mu_1(K,\Lambda)^n\operatorname{vol}(K)\geq\frac{1}{n!}\det(\Lambda),
$$

and equality can occur only when $K$ is a crosspolytope. This conjecture is presented as a polar analogue of Minkowski's first fundamental theorem and remains unresolved in the source.
record.source_name: Bernardo González Merino and Matthias Henze, “On densities of lattice arrangements intersecting every i-dimensional affine subspace”, arXiv:1605.00443 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.00443

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

record.title: The conjecture on the maximum of the GFF on the circle
record.statement:
Let $V_N$ be the maximum of the discretized Gaussian free field on the circle with singularity parameter $\alpha\geq 0$. Let $M_{(\tau=1,\alpha,\alpha)}$ denote the critical Morris integral distribution, and let $X,Y,Y'$ be the Barnes beta variables defined in the conjecture. **Maximum of the GFF on the circle.** As $N\to\infty$,

$$
\mathbf{E}[e^{qV_N}]\approx e^{q(2\log N-(3/2)\log\log N+\operatorname{const})}\mathbf{E}[M_{(\tau=1,\alpha,\alpha)}^q],
$$

and $V_N$ has the stated decomposition into the deterministic centering, $\log X+\log Y+\log Y'+o(1)$. When $\alpha=0$, the $\log X$ term is absent and $Y$ and $Y'$ have the same law. The claim extends the conjecture of Fyodorov and Bouchaud from $\alpha=0$ to general $\alpha$; no resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Dmitry Ostrovsky, “On Barnes Beta Distributions and Applications to the Maximum Distribution of the 2D Gaussian Free Field”, arXiv:1605.01589 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.01589

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

record.title: The freezing hypothesis for the exponential functional of the GFF
record.statement:
Let $X$ be the normalized exponential functional introduced in the source, and let $q$ be in the range where the displayed moments exist. **Freezing hypothesis.** For $\beta>1$,

$$
\mathbf{E}\left[X^{q/\beta}\right]\Gamma\left(1-\frac q\beta\right)=\left.\mathbf{E}\left[X^{q/\beta}\right]\Gamma\left(1-\frac q\beta\right)\right|_{\beta=1}.
$$

This is the freezing assumption that extends the high-temperature expression beyond the critical point and underlies the proposed maximum-distribution asymptotics. It was formulated in earlier work on logarithmically correlated fields; the supplied text does not establish it.

record.title: The augmented Zagreb index–atom-bond connectivity index extremal tree conjecture
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $n$ vertices. The augmented Zagreb index $AZI$ and the atom-bond connectivity index $ABC$ are graph invariants of $T$.

**Extremal tree conjecture.** The $n$-vertex tree $T$ has the maximum $AZI$ value if and only if $T$ has the minimum $ABC$ index.

This conjecture proposes that the trees maximizing the augmented Zagreb index are exactly the trees minimizing the atom-bond connectivity index. The source presents it as an open conjecture; no resolution is given there.
record.source_name: Akbar Ali and Akhlaq Ahmad Bhatti, “A note on the augmented Zagreb index of cacti with fixed number of vertices and cycles”, arXiv:1605.01888 (2016).

record.title: The stable homotopy type determines the move-equivalence class of a framed flow category
record.statement: Let $(\mathscr{C}_1,\iota_1,\varphi_1)$ and $(\mathscr{C}_2,\iota_2,\varphi_2)$ be framed flow categories. Their associated stable homotopy types are the stable homotopy types determined by the corresponding realizations $\mathcal{X}(\mathscr{C}_1)$ and $\mathcal{X}(\mathscr{C}_2)$. **Stable homotopy type conjecture.** If the two framed flow categories determine the same stable homotopy type, then they are move equivalent to one another. The preceding corollary establishes this when the reduced homology with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ is supported in two consecutive degrees, while the general assertion is suggested as a stronger statement.

record.title: Connected forcing number lower bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with minimum degree $\delta$ and girth $g$, and let $F_c(G)$ denote its connected forcing number.

**Connected forcing number lower bound conjecture.**

$$
F_c(G) \ge \delta + (\delta - 2)(g - 3).
$$

This is a weaker version of the original lower-bound conjecture for the forcing number $F(G)$, because $F(G) \le F_c(G)$. The original conjecture remains open, and this connected-forcing version is presented as an open problem.
record.source_name: Randy Davila, Michael Henning, Colton Magnant and Ryan Pepper, “Bounds on the connected forcing number of a graph”, arXiv:1605.02124 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.02124

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2016). “Since $F(G)$ is at most $F_c(G)$, and since the original conjecture remains open, we present the following weaker conjecture.”

record.title: The MDS conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field, and let $[n,k]$ denote a linear code of length $n$ and dimension $k$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. If $1<k<q$, then

$$
n\le q+1,
$$

except when $q$ is even and $k=3$ or $k=q-1$, in which cases

$$
n\le q+2.
$$

The conjecture gives the expected maximum length of nontrivial maximum-distance-separable codes over finite fields. The paper uses known results in substantial parameter ranges, while the general assertion is presented as the MDS conjecture.
record.source_name: Jun Zhang and Daqing Wan, “On Deep Holes of Projective Reed-Solomon Codes”, arXiv:1605.02423 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.02423

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2016). “This conjecture remains open, but has been proved in if either $k+1\le p$ or $3\le q-p+1\le k+1\le q-2$.”

record.title: Realization of the amenable radical by a random-walk subgroup
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finitely generated group. For a probability measure $\mu$ on $G$, let $A_\mu$ denote the associated subgroup, and let the amenable radical be the largest amenable normal subgroup of $G$. **Amenable-radical realization conjecture.** There exists some probability measure $\mu$ on $G$ such that

$$
A_\mu=\text{the amenable radical of }G.
$$

This is presented as a stronger or more desirable formulation concerning whether the amenable radical can be exactly recovered from a suitable random walk. The supplied text does not specify additional conditions on $\mu$ or give evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Murray Elder and Cameron Rogers, “On a theorem of Avez”, arXiv:1605.04065 (2017).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.04065

record.title: Brualdi–Stein hypergraph matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H$ be an $n$-regular $3$-partite hypergraph with sides $A$, $B$, and $C$, each of size $n$. A pair of sides is **simple** if no pair of vertices from those sides belongs to more than one edge, and let $\nu(H)$ denote the maximum size of a matching in $H$. **Brualdi–Stein hypergraph conjecture.** If all three pairs $(A,B)$, $(B,C)$, and $(A,C)$ are simple, then

$$
\nu(H)\ge n-1.
$$

This is the hypergraph formulation of the partial-transversal conjecture for Latin squares and remains open in this generality.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Dani Kotlar and Ran Ziv, “Degree conditions for matchability in 3-partite hypergraphs”, arXiv:1605.05667 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.05667

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

record.title: Asymmetric degree conjecture for 3-partite hypergraph matchings
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a simple $3$-partite hypergraph with sides $A$, $B$, and $C$. Write $\delta(A)$ for the minimum degree of a vertex in $A$, $\Delta(B\cup C)$ for the maximum degree of a vertex in $B\cup C$, and let $\nu(H)$ be the maximum matching size. **Asymmetric degree conjecture.** The following assertions should hold:

1. If $d=\delta(A)\ge \Delta(B\cup C)$, then

$$
\nu(H)\ge \frac{d-1}{d}|A|.
$$

2. If

$$
\delta(A)\ge \max\bigl(\Delta(B\cup C),2|A|-1\bigr),
$$

then

$$
\nu(H)=|A|.
$$

This formulation is intended to capture the essence of the regular conjecture in an asymmetric setting; the paper gives only partial results.
record.source_name: Ron Aharoni, Eli Berger, Dani Kotlar and Ran Ziv, “Degree conditions for matchability in 3-partite hypergraphs”, arXiv:1605.05667 (2016).
record.references:

record.title: Degree version of the Erdős hypergraph matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. Write $\delta_1(H)$ for its minimum vertex degree, and say that a matching has size $s$ when it consists of $s$ vertex-disjoint edges. Let $s,k,n$ be positive integers with $s<n/k$. **Degree Erdős matching conjecture.** If

$$
\delta_1(H)>\binom{n-1}{k-1}-\binom{n-s}{k-1},
$$

then $H$ contains a matching of size $s$. This conjectures that the degree threshold attained by the hypergraph consisting of all $k$-sets meeting a fixed set of $s-1$ vertices remains extremal whenever $n>ks$. The paper proves the corresponding result when $n\ge 3k^2s$ and notes that the general case remains open; the case $n=ks$ is excluded.
record.source_name: Hao Huang and Yi Zhao, “Degree versions of the Erdos-Ko-Rado Theorem and Erdos hypergraph matching conjecture”, arXiv:1605.07535 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.07535

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

record.title: The orbit-method quantization conjecture for nilpotent orbit covers
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a complex simple Lie group with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$, and let $K$ be a maximal compact subgroup of $G$ with complexification $K_{\mathbb{C}}$. For a nilpotent orbit $\mathcal{O}$, let $R(\mathcal{O})$ be its ring of regular functions. For $e
ein\mathcal{O}$, let $G_e$ be its isotropy group, let $(G_e)^0$ be the identity component, and define $A(\mathcal{O})=G_e/(G_e)^0$. For an irreducible representation $\rho$ of $A(\mathcal{O})$, let $R(\mathcal{O},\rho)$ denote the global sections of the $G$-equivariant bundle $G\times_{G_e}V_{\rho}\to G/G_e\cong\mathcal{O}$. **The orbit-method quantization conjecture.** There exists a (not necessarily unique) $(\mathfrak{g}_{\mathbb{C}},K_{\mathbb{C}})$-module $Q$ such that

$$
Q|_{K_{\mathbb{C}}}\cong R(\mathcal{O}),
$$

and, more generally, for every irreducible representation $\rho$ of $A(\mathcal{O})$, there exists a $(\mathfrak{g}_{\mathbb{C}},K_{\mathbb{C}})$-module $Q_{\rho}$ such that

$$
Q_{\rho}|_{K_{\mathbb{C}}}\cong R(\mathcal{O},\rho)=\operatorname{Ind}_{G^e}^{G}(\rho).
$$

When $\rho$ is trivial, $R(\mathcal{O},\rho)=R(\mathcal{O})$. This is the orbit-method prediction for quantizing nilpotent orbits and their equivariant local systems; the source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Kayue Daniel Wong, “Some Calculations of the Lusztig-Vogan Bijection for Classical Nilpotent Orbits”, arXiv:1605.09575 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.09575

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

record.title: Boundary regularity conjecture for the Liouville density of the discrete Gaussian free field
record.statement: Let $D$ be a domain, let $t\in\mathbb R$, and let $\rho^D(t,\mathord\cdot)$ denote the density from Theorem 2.7. **Boundary regularity conjecture.** For each $t\in\mathbb R$, the function $x\mapsto\rho^D(t,x)$ is bounded and tends to zero as $x$ approaches $\partial D$. In particular, the function admits a continuous extension to all of $\overline D$. The preceding results establish absolute continuity of the relevant measure and an integrability condition for this density, but do not determine its boundary regularity; the conjecture is motivated by the stated asymptotics and simulations.
record.source_name: Marek Biskup and Oren Louidor, “Full extremal process, cluster law and freezing for the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian Free Field”, arXiv:1606.00510 (2018).

record.title: Grading conjecture for generalized minors on triple flag configurations
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a reductive group, let $\omega_{i_l}$ be fundamental weights, and let $u_l$ be the Weyl-group elements indexing the functions $\Delta_{u_l\omega_{i_l},\omega_{i_l}}$ on $\operatorname{Conf}_3 \mathcal{A}_G$. The algebra $\mathcal{O}(\operatorname{Conf}_3 \mathcal{A}_G)$ is graded by dominant weights of $G$. **Grading conjecture.** Each of the functions $\Delta_{u_l\omega_{i_l},\omega_{i_l}}$ lies in a single graded piece

$$
[V_{\lambda} \otimes V_{\mu} \otimes V_{\nu}]^G
$$

for some dominant weights $\lambda,\mu,\nu$. This conjecture is needed to determine the quiver arrows connecting edge functions to face functions; the source gives no resolution or further evidence about its status.

record.title: The triangle-free average-to-maximum independent set ratio conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a triangle-free graph. Write $4\alpha(G)4$ for its maximum independent set size and $4\overline{\alpha}_G(1)4$ for the average size of an independent set in the hard-core model at fugacity $1$.

**Average-to-maximum ratio conjecture.**

$$
\frac{\alpha(G)}{\overline{\alpha}_G(1)} \ge \frac{4}{3}.
$$

Replacing $4/3$ by any constant strictly greater than $1$ would improve the known upper bound on $R(3,k)$. The conjecture is motivated by the gap between maximum and average independent set size in triangle-free graphs; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ewan Davies, Matthew Jenssen, Will Perkins and Barnaby Roberts, “On the average size of independent sets in triangle-free graphs”, arXiv:1606.01043 (2017).

record.title: The subobject morphism conjecture for overconvergent F-isocrystals
record.statement: Let $X$ be the fixed variety, and let $\operatorname{\mathbf{F-Isoc}}(X)$ and $\operatorname{\mathbf{F-Isoc}}^\dagger(X)$ denote the categories of convergent and overconvergent $F$-isocrystals on $X$. Let $\mathcal{E}_1,\mathcal{E}_2 \in \operatorname{\mathbf{F-Isoc}}^\dagger(X)$ be irreducible, and let $\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F}_2$ be objects of $\operatorname{\mathbf{F-Isoc}}(X)$ that are subobjects of $\mathcal{E}_1,\mathcal{E}_2$, respectively. **Subobject morphism conjecture.** For every morphism $\mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2$ in $\operatorname{\mathbf{F-Isoc}}(X)$, there exists a morphism $\mathcal{E}_1 \to \mathcal{E}_2$ in $\operatorname{\mathbf{F-Isoc}}^\dagger(X)$ such that the induced diagram commutes in $\operatorname{\mathbf{F-Isoc}}(X)$. This optimistic conjecture would control how morphisms between convergent subobjects extend in the overconvergent category. An important special case says that an irreducible overconvergent $F$-isocrystal with constant slope polygon is uniquely determined by the first step of its slope filtration; no counterexample is known.
record.source_name: Kiran S. Kedlaya, “Notes on isocrystals”, arXiv:1606.01321 (2022).

record.title: Alternating expansion conjecture for Young quasisymmetric Schur functions of distinct-part partitions
record.statement:
Let $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\ldots,\lambda_k)$ be a partition whose $k$ parts are all distinct. For $\sigma\in S_k$, define

$$
\sigma(\lambda)=(\lambda_{\sigma(1)},\lambda_{\sigma(2)},\ldots,\lambda_{\sigma(k)}),
$$

and let $\ell(\sigma)$ be the length of $\sigma$, namely the minimum number of adjacent transpositions $(i,i+1)$ needed to generate it. **Alternating expansion conjecture.** One has

$$
\hat{\mathscr{S}}_\lambda=\sum_{\sigma\in S_k}(-1)^{\ell(\sigma)}\mathfrak{S}^*_{\sigma(\lambda)}.
$$

The formula gives an explicit signed expansion into dual immaculate quasisymmetric functions for partitions with distinct parts; it is presented as a conjecture based on the authors' computations, and no proof or resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Edward E. Allen, Joshua Hallam and Sarah K. Mason, “Dual Immaculate Quasisymmetric Functions Expand Positively into Young Quasisymmetric Schur Functions”, arXiv:1606.03519 (2016).

record.title: The linear greedy defining set conjecture for Latin squares
record.statement:
Let $g_n$ be the cardinality of a smallest greedy defining set among all $n\times n$ Latin squares, with greedy defining sets taken in lexicographic order. **Linear greedy defining set conjecture.** The function $g_n$ satisfies

$$
g_n={\mathcal{O}}(n).
$$

This conjecture was attributed to Z3 and is stated as still unsolved in the source, although it has been proved for some infinite sequences of natural numbers.
record.source_name: Manouchehr Zaker, “First-Fit coloring of Cartesian product graphs and its defining sets”, arXiv:1606.05480 (2016).

record.title: Universal bounded-degree graph conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal H(n,\Delta)$ be the family of all graphs on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta$. A graph $G$ is **$\mathcal F$-universal** if it contains every member of a graph family $\mathcal F$. Let $G_{n,p}$ be the binomial random graph.

**Universal bounded-degree graph conjecture.** Let $\Delta\in\mathbb N$ and $p=\omega\left(n^{-1}\log^{1/\Delta}n\right)^{\frac{2}{\Delta+1}}$. Then, with high probability, $G_{n,p}$ is $\mathcal H(n,\Delta)$-universal.

This strengthens the preceding embedding conjecture by requiring one random graph to contain every graph on $n$ vertices of maximum degree at most $\Delta$. The proposed density is motivated by the conjectured worst case of $K_{\Delta+1}$-factors, but the statement remains open in the source.
record.source_name: Asaf Ferber, Kyle Luh and Oanh Nguyen, “Embedding large graphs into a random graph”, arXiv:1606.05923 (2017).

record.title: The strict MMS star conjecture for Latin squares of order 7
record.statement:
A Latin square of order $7$ is considered with its associated incidence structure. It has the **strict MMS star property** when the stars are the only sets of intersecting lines of maximum size under the relevant MMS condition.

**Strict MMS star conjecture for order 7.** Any Latin square of order $7$ has the strict MMS star property.

The source presents this as a conjecture following the discussion of small Latin squares and gives no resolution evidence. Its status is therefore open.
record.source_name: Ferdinand Ihringer and Karen Meagher, “Manickam-Miklós-Singhi Conjectures on Partial Geometries”, arXiv:1606.06275 (2017).

record.title: Conjectured exponential stability bound for the permanent near maximal row norm
record.statement:
Let $A$ be an $n\times n$ matrix with complex entries, and let $h_\infty$ denote the maximum modulus of an entry of $A$. Assume that

$$
\Vert A\Vert_2\leq 1.
$$

**Exponential stability conjecture.** There is some constant $C>0$ and some polynomial $f(n)$ such that

$$
|\operatorname{per}(A)|\leq f(n)e^{-Cn(1-h_\infty)}.
$$

The preceding theorem gives an exponential bound when $1-h_\infty$ is not too small, while the conjecture is intended to capture the sharper behavior when $h_\infty$ is close to $1$; the source does not state that this conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Ross Berkowitz and Pat Devlin, “A stability result using the matrix norm to bound the permanent”, arXiv:1606.07474 (2016).

record.title: The maximum-degree bound for lazy cop number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, let $\Delta$ be its maximum degree, and let $c_L(G)$ denote its lazy cop number.

**Maximum-degree conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta\geq n-k^2,
$$

then

$$
c_L(G)\leq k.
$$

The statement is proposed as a natural generalization of the paper's proved bound for maximum degree at least $n-9$. The source suggests that it would follow inductively from the rook graph conjecture, but does not establish it.

record.title: Block structure conjecture for graphs avoiding consecutive even cycle lengths
record.statement: Let $t\geq1$ and let $G$ be a graph with a maximum number of edges among graphs that do not contain cycles of $t$ consecutive even lengths. A **block** is a maximal connected subgraph with no cut vertex. **Block structure conjecture.** Every block of $G$ is a complete graph of order at most $2t+1$. The conjecture is stated as a strengthening of Thomassen's conjecture and is known in the source only for $t=1$; its general case remains open.
record.source_name: Benny Sudakov and Jacques Verstraete, “The extremal function for cycles of length mod k”, arXiv:1606.08532 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08532

record.title: The positive EH-coefficient conjecture for tournaments
record.statement:
A **tournament** is a directed graph with exactly one directed edge between each pair of distinct vertices. For a tournament $S$, a nonnegative real number $\epsilon$ is an **EH-coefficient** if there exists $c>0$ such that every $S$-free tournament $T$ satisfies $\alpha(T)\geq c|V(T)|^\epsilon$, where $\alpha(T)$ is the maximum size of a transitive subtournament.

**Positive EH-coefficient conjecture.** Every tournament has a positive EH-coefficient.

The source states that this is equivalent to the Erdős–Hajnal conjecture. Introducing the constant $c$ removes effects from tournaments of bounded order; the conjecture remains open in general.
record.source_name: Maria Chudnovsky, “The Erdös-Hajnal Conjecture—A Survey”, arXiv:1606.08827 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.08827

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2016). “In fact, what is really proved in is the following: Every bull-free graph is $2$-narrow.”

record.title: Burton's conjecture on intersections of normal-surface-theory fans
record.statement:
For $d\geq2$, let $U(d,k)$ denote the maximum number of inclusion-maximal cones in the intersection of $k$ balanced fans in general position in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where each fan consists of three halfplane cones with a common axis. **Burton's conjecture.** The maximum for $k=d-1$ satisfies

$$
U(d,d-1)=1+2^{d-1}.
$$

The source states that its Minkowski-sum results resolve this conjecture, so the claim is solved.
record.source_name: Karim Adiprasito, Philip Brinkmann, Arnau Padrol, Pavel Paták, Zuzana Patáková and Raman Sanyal, “Colorful simplicial depth, Minkowski sums, and generalized Gale transforms”, arXiv:1607.00347 (2016).
record.references:

record.title: Minimum trace-distance contraction conjecture for qubit channels over a fixed classical channel
record.statement:
Let $a,f\in[0,1]$ and let $\mathcal{Q}_{\mathbb{C}}(a,f)$ denote the set of qubit channels over the classical channel

$$
\begin{pmatrix}
1-a & a\\\\
1-f & f
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

For a qubit channel $Q$, let $\eta^{\operatorname{Tr}}(Q)$ be its trace-distance contraction coefficient. **Minimum trace-distance contraction conjecture.**

$$
\inf\left\\{\eta^{\operatorname{Tr}}(Q):Q\in\mathcal{Q}_{\mathbb{C}}(a,f)\right\\}=|a-f|.
$$

This value is the trace-distance contraction coefficient of the underlying classical channel. The paper establishes the corresponding supremum but leaves this infimum conjectural.
record.source_name: Attila Lovas and Attila Andai, “Volume of the space of qubit channels and some new results about the distribution of the quantum Dobrushin coefficient”, arXiv:1607.01215 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.01215

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2016).

record.title: A fully supported local information maximum on the full two-shift
record.statement: Let $(X,T)$ be the full two-shift, let $\alpha$ be the partition used to define information, and consider the space of one-step Markov measures on $X$. A measure is fully supported when every allowed cylinder has positive measure, and a local maximum is understood relative to this space. **Fully supported local-maximum conjecture.** There is a fully supported one-step Markov measure that is a local maximum of $\operatorname{Int}_\mu(X,T,\alpha)$ among all one-step Markov measures. The assertion is suggested by numerical computations in the source; no proof or resolution is supplied.
record.source_name: Karl Petersen, “Measuring Complexity in Cantor Dynamics”, arXiv:1607.02425 (2016).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2016). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1512.01143](https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.01143).

record.title: Equality conjecture for local Petrovskii lacuna counts
record.statement:
Let $f_0:{\mathbb R}^{N-2}\to{\mathbb R}$ be a parabolic critical point, and consider a versal deformation of $f_0$. Table 1 gives, for each singularity and parity case, either an exact number of holomorphic local lacunas or an upper or lower bound for their number.

**Equality conjecture.** In every cell of Table 1, except possibly the cell corresponding to $X_9^2$, each inequality can be replaced by an equality.

The theorem preceding this conjecture establishes the listed exact values and bounds, with some bounds having only computer proofs. The conjecture concerns whether the remaining inequalities are sharp; the source gives no resolution status.

record.title: Halfspace meta-conjecture for extremal families with bounded matching number
record.statement:
Let $\alpha_1\ge\alpha_2\ge\cdots\ge\alpha_n\ge0$ be real numbers with $\sum_i\alpha_i<s$, and write $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n)$. Define

$$
\mathcal F(\boldsymbol\alpha):=\Bigl\{F\in2^{[n]}:\sum_{i\in F}\alpha_i\ge1\Bigr\}.
$$

Then $\nu(\mathcal F(\boldsymbol\alpha))<s$.

**Halfspace meta-conjecture.** For any $n,s$, the maximum defining $e(n,s)$ is attained by $\mathcal F(\boldsymbol\alpha)$ for a suitable $\boldsymbol\alpha\in\mathbb R^n$.

The conjecture proposes that every extremal nonuniform family can be represented as the intersection of the Boolean cube with a weighted halfspace. The paper observes that the principal constructions discussed there have this form, but gives no resolution for the general assertion.

record.title: Gyárfás–Lehel Tree Packing Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $T_1,\dotsc,T_n$ be trees, and let $v(T_i)$ denote the number of vertices of $T_i$. A collection of graphs **packs** into a graph $G$ if there are edge-disjoint subgraphs of $G$ isomorphic to the graphs in the collection. **Tree Packing Conjecture.** Any collection $T_1,\dotsc,T_n$ of trees with

$$
v(T_i)=i
$$

for each $i$ packs into the complete graph $K_n$. This conjecture concerns packing trees of all sizes into a graph whose order matches the largest tree; its relationship with Ringel's related tree-packing conjecture makes it a central problem in graph decomposition.

record.title: The Ax-Schanuel conjecture for mixed Shimura varieties
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a connected mixed Shimura variety associated with $(P,\mathcal{X}^+)$ and let $\mathrm{unif}\colon\mathcal{X}^+\to S$ be its uniformization. Let $\mathbscr{Z}$ be the graph of the restriction of $\mathrm{unif}$ to a complex analytic irreducible subvariety $\widetilde{Z}$, and let $\mathbscr{B}$ be its Zariski closure in $\mathcal{X}^+\times S$. Let $F$ be the smallest bi-algebraic, equivalently weakly special, subvariety of $S$ containing $Z=\operatorname{pr}_S(\mathbscr{Z})$. **Ax-Schanuel conjecture for mixed Shimura varieties.** Then

$$
\dim\mathbscr{B}-\dim\mathbscr{Z}\geqslant\dim F.
$$

This is stated as a common generalization of the Ax logarithmique and Ax–Lindemann theorems for mixed Shimura varieties; the supplied text does not state that it has been proved.

record.title: Thin-position conjecture for the knots $K_{2,1,3,7}$ and $K_{4,1,3,3}$
record.statement: Let $B_i$ be the braids occurring in the paper's construction, and let $K_{2,1,3,7}$ and $K_{4,1,3,3}$ denote the corresponding knots. A thin position is an embedding realizing minimum width; minimum trunk and bridge number are defined analogously. **Thin-position conjecture.** For sufficiently complicated braids $B_i$, thin position of $K_{2,1,3,7}$ does not realize minimum trunk or minimum bridge number, while thin position of $K_{4,1,3,3}$ realizes minimum bridge number but not minimum trunk. These claims arise from embeddings whose thinness cannot currently be verified for the stated examples, so they remain conjectural.

record.title: The monotonicity conjecture for percolation time in finite projective planes
record.statement:
Let $\Pi_q$ be a finite projective plane of order $q$, let $T_r(\Pi_q)$ denote the maximum percolation time among percolating sets at infection rate $r$, and let $r_1$ and $r_2$ be infection rates. **Percolation-time monotonicity conjecture.** If

$$
r_1<r_2,
$$

then

$$
T_{r_1}(\Pi_q)\leq T_{r_2}(\Pi_q).
$$

The conjecture proposes that the slowest possible percolation does not become faster as the infection rate increases. The source motivates it with exhaustive searches and random experiments, but explicitly says that the belief is not justified; no resolution is supplied.

record.title: The maximum-degree-three zero forcing conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$ and maximum degree $3$. The **zero forcing number** $Z(G)$ is the minimum size of a set of vertices from which all vertices can be obtained by repeatedly adding the unique neighbor outside the current set of a vertex inside it.

**Maximum-degree-three zero forcing conjecture.**

$$
Z(G)\leq \frac{1}{3}n+2.
$$

The conjecture would considerably improve the known general upper bound for graphs of maximum degree $3$. The paper proves a weaker bound for connected graphs of maximum degree $3$ and girth at least $5$, but the stated conjecture remains open in the supplied source.

record.title: Deficiency bounds for complete graphs of power-of-two order
record.statement:
Let $q\in\mathbb{Z}_+$, let $K_{2^{q+1}+1}$ be the complete graph on $2^{q+1}+1$ vertices, and let $w_{def}(G)$ and $W_{def}(G)$ denote the minimum and maximum, respectively, of the number of colors in a proper edge-coloring of $G$ having minimum deficiency.

**Complete-graph deficiency conjecture.** For any $q\in\mathbb{Z}_+$,

$$
w_{def}\left(K_{2^{q+1}+1}\right)=W_{def}\left(K_{2^{q+1}+1}\right)=3\cdot2^q.
$$

The conjecture is motivated by the inability to find a proper edge-coloring of these complete graphs with more than $3\cdot2^q$ colors having minimum deficiency. It remains open in the supplied source.

record.title: The component-star conjecture for disconnected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a disconnected graph whose components are all isomorphic to a graph $H$, and let $ern(G)$ be the minimum number of edge-cards needed to determine $G$ up to isomorphism. **Component-star conjecture.** If $ern(G)>3$, then $H$ is isomorphic to the star $K_{1,r}$, where $r$ is the number of edges of $H$.

The conjecture is attributed in the surrounding discussion to Asciak and Lauri and is motivated by computational evidence and bounds for disconnected graphs. The supplied text does not report a resolution.

record.title: The infinite-class conjecture for trees with edge-reconstruction number three
record.statement:
Let $ern(T)$ denote the minimum number of edge-cards needed to determine a tree $T$ up to isomorphism. The relevant infinite families are the paths on an odd number of vertices, the caterpillars $\langle 2,0,\ldots,0,2\rangle$ of even diameter, and the family of trees $T_k$ described in the paper. **Infinite-class conjecture.** These are the only infinite classes of trees having $ern(T)=3$.

This conjecture is attributed to Asciak, Lauri, Myrvold, and Pannone and is based on computer searches together with known examples. The supplied text does not report a resolution.

record.title: The degree-associated edge-reconstruction conjecture for disconnected equal-component graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be as in Theorem 4.2: a disconnected graph whose non-trivial components are all isomorphic to a graph $H$. Let $dern(G)$ denote the minimum number of degree-associated edge-cards needed to determine $G$ up to isomorphism. **Equal-component degree-associated edge-reconstruction conjecture.** If the hypothesis $\delta(H)\geq 3$ in Theorem 4.2 is replaced by the exclusions

$$
H\neq K_{1,3},\qquad H\neq K_{1,2},\qquad H\neq K_{2,3},
$$

then $dern(G)\leq 2$.

The conjecture is motivated by the observation that the three excluded component types give the exceptional examples known in the discussion, while the stated bound is proved under the stronger minimum-degree condition. Its general status is left open in the supplied text.

record.title: Polynomial-time computation of fixed points and spectral norms for nonsingular symmetric tensors
record.statement: Fix $n\in\mathord{\mathbb N}$ with $2<n$, and let ${\cal S}\in\mathrm{S}^d\mathord{\mathbb C}^n$ be nonsingular. Let $\mathbf H$ denote the polynomial map whose fixed points are used to compute the spectral norm of ${\cal S}$. **Nonsingular fixed-point computation conjecture.** With probability $1$, all fixed points of $\mathbf H$ can be found within $\varepsilon$ approximation in time polynomial in $d$; in particular, $\|{\cal S}\|_{\sigma}$ can be computed within $\varepsilon$ approximation in time polynomial in $d$, with probability $1$. The conjecture arises from applying homotopy methods to the $(d-1)^{2n}$ fixed points associated with a nonsingular tensor. It remains open in the supplied text.

record.title: The logarithmic diameter conjecture for the SPA model giant component
record.statement:
Let $m=2$ and let $p,A_1
in(0,1)$ be parameters of the SPA model, with $A_2$ chosen sufficiently large. The **giant component** is the largest connected component of the graph produced by this model. **Logarithmic diameter conjecture.** For each choice of $p,A_1\in(0,1)$, and for large enough choice of $A_2$, asymptotically almost surely the giant component of a graph produced by the SPA model with parameters $A_1,A_2,p$ and $m=2$ has diameter $O(\log n)$. This would sharpen the proved $O(\log^2 n)$ effective-diameter bound for the corresponding model with $p=1$, establishing a logarithmic bound for the diameter of the giant component; the statement is left open.
